analyst.summary: LIC's FY26 numbers show a genuine margin-quality improvement wrapped inside a still-declining, if decelerating, market-share story. VNB grew 41.63% to Rs 14,179 crore with margin up 360bps to 21.2% (25.7% in Q4 alone), powered by a real shift toward non-par products (43.78% APE growth, now 53% of total VNB) -- the highest-quality print of LIC's listed history. Against that, total premium market share slipped again (56.66% FY26 vs 57.05% FY25, part of a slide from ~66% in FY22), distribution stays 91.8% agency-dependent into an IRDAI surrender-value regime that structurally squeezes early-lapse economics, and a phased government OFS (targeting the SEBI 75% public-float floor, an estimated ~Rs 1.28 lakh crore of stock still to sell) is a recurring supply overhang. At roughly 0.70x embedded value (mcap ~Rs 5.54 lakh crore vs IEV Rs 7.89 lakh crore), the market prices close to run-off value for the in-force book with little credit for a VNB engine compounding at 40%+ -- a discount that looks moderately too punitive given the margin trajectory, but not obviously mispriced given the ongoing, mechanical OFS supply that will cap re-rating pace regardless of fundamentals. Hold.
